text_fidelity_a:
Asobu Bumper Bottle Double Wall Glass Bottle with Tea Infuser and Bumpers I ran into quite a few issues when I used this for the first time, so let me share some of the lessons I learned. First, it's much better using the strainer/infuser as a strainer. When I tried to use it as an infuser, I could only fill the bottle halfway because the tea had completely blocked the holes. Also it becomes very difficult to take the infuser out (which is already a very difficult feat since it fits so tightly) with tea in the way of the handle. These inconveniences make me give it three stars because putting tea into the body of the bottle limits what type of tea can be used. Black and green teas will oversteep and get bitter, so you're basically constricted to herbal and fruit teas. If that's all you want it for, then this bottle should not pose a problem for you.

I received this bottle at a discount for my honest and unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: Asobu Bumper Bottle Double Wall Glass Bottle with Tea Infuser and Bumpers

The straps that are on the underside to attach it to the bike rack are crap.  They are too long.  The velcro is placed too far away so that if you pull it to the tightness you need, the velcro misses itself entirely.  That pretty much renders it useless.  I've tried numerous fixes, short of cutting the strap and sewing it back together shorter, mostly because I don't have a sewing machine which you would need with the kind of pressure you have to put on it to make it tight.  Another thing is the placement of these straps makes it anything but quick release and quick re-attach.  As I live in a large city, I have to take the bag with me whenever I make a stop, and fiddling around underneath with hard to reach attachment points adds way more time to each stop.  The third thing is that those straps are of very poor quality.  The weave is loose and they are flimsy.  Which is strange because everything else about this bike bag is very well-made and well-designed.  In the final analysis, I gave up, attached a milk crate to the back of my bike, and I throw this bike bag in it.  Which pretty much invalidates the panier function I wanted. text_fidelity_a:
Becko 47 Inches Auto Open Umbrella Long Umbrella with 16 Ribs, Durable and Strong Enough for the Fierce Wind and Heavy Rain, Classic Style with Soft Foam Rubber Stick Handle, Unisex Umbrella This is an outstanding umbrella. I know it must sound silly to be so gushy about an umbrella, but I have never found a foldable umbrella that offered decent performance. This works just as well as my full-size umbrella with the huge benefit of being able to be folded up and carried in a briefcase.

The build quality is excellent, with well-made seams on the canopy, and very sturdy ribs. The automatic pop-up action is solid and quick to operate. The auto fold-up ability is equally well-done (e.g., you can push the “close” button and the canopy folds up, making it far easier to deal with once you’ve entered a building).

Wind resistance is quite good, with vent flaps that work well to prevent blowouts. The vents have a good amount of fabric overlap to keep any rain from getting through.

text_fidelity_a: Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash – PS1543 - Stand up Paddle Board Hook-and-Loop System with Comfortable Neoprene Padding at Ankle My wife and I recently got a couple of inflatable SUPs to take out - we had done some SUP and kayak tours and wanted to go out on our own. To that end, we also decided to grab this Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash when I had the chance. The SUPs came with leashes, but I’d heard the Pelican brand was pretty good and one thing we experienced on the tours was rubbing from the leashes. We both have backgrounds as athletes, which also includes injuries and the like, and as we age, we find that comfort is as important to us as anything. And the rubbing we had experienced was enough to consider not even going out again. So... we wanted leashes that would feel good. This Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash feels very good. Now we haven’t been out on the water (our state requires flotation devices that we haven’t gotten yet, and weather has kept us off), but we put this (and another Pelican leash) through some tests here at home and come away feeling very positive. This leash comes in two parts: the main structure and the green-yellow band that connects directly to the SUP D Ring. You loop that, then it velcro onto the main unit - pay attention to how you take it out to know more quickly how to get it back into the velcro. We can’t figure out if this or the other (a single piece) is better, but at this point, we feel like they both have a strong argument for why they each are good/better, and in the end, for us, it’s a wash. So that brings us to the comfort. This Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash has a great feeling ankle wrap. Once on it didn’t rub - we tried it at varying tightnesses and positions - and tried a lot of different things to see if it would rub or bother us. We both found it really comfortable and stayed solidly in place. There are two rotating anchors - meaning it turns easy and does not twist or wrap or ... it moves and doesn’t get stuck or do that thing like old fashioned phone lines that - remember - were become a twisted mess. This Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash is great at getting wherever you need it so it’s not in the way, and it stays in place, feels great, and we both think, is going to make being on the water a fun and comfortable experience. So happy to have this Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash and really liking the Pelican brand.

text_fidelity_a:
Travel Kuppe Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Cycling Sports Water Bottle, Includes Both Straw and Sip Lid If you must have a steel water bottle on your bicycle (for health or other reasons), this may be for you. However, there are many disadvantages. First, this bottle is big - about 1 inch taller than a 24 ounce plastic water bottle, even though the capacity is a smaller 20 ounces. Of course, this bottle is less efficient with space because of the insulation feature. The extra height will cause problems with smaller bicycles, especially in the seat tube water bottle cage. While the straw cap seems interesting, in practice this is useless on a bicycle. With the straw open, the bottle will not fit on my bicycle. With the straw closed, you need 2 hands to open the straw, which is dangerous while riding your bicycle. There are plastic insulated bicycle water bottles on the market that are much cheaper and lighter weight than this (eg Polar or Camelbak) and they don't need the straw since you can just squeeze them to squirt the water out.

This bottle is also very heavy - 11.5 ounces compared to 3 ounces for a standard plastic water bottle. Gripping this bottle is much more difficult than a plastic bottle since (1) it is slippery when wet and (2) it doesn't squeeze when gripped like a plastic bottle. I do not recommend using this bottle with metal water bottle cages since it rattles like crazy; a plastic water bottle cage may be better, especially if it has a grippy interior.

The insulation does work, but you only have 20 ounces of water in there so if you drink that in the first hour of your ride, can you refill the bottle with more cold water or just with tap water that isn't cold enough to be worth insulating? If you're not drinking at least 20 ounces per hour on a day that is hot enough to need an insulated water bottle, you are not drinking enough to avoid dehydration.

As a bicycle water bottle, I give this only 2 stars because of all the limitations. For use in a car's cup holder or similar it may work better, but then you're competing with dozens of other steel water bottles that cost much less, so I give it 2 stars for that use case as well.
text_fidelity_b: Travel Kuppe Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Cycling Sports Water Bottle, Includes Both Straw and Sip Lid

text_fidelity_a:
High Sierra Access Laptop Backpack I compared 4 High Sierra backpack models: Access (this model), Neo [[ASIN:B007E7160K High Sierra Neo Backpack]], Mayhem [[ASIN:B007E722MG High Sierra Mayhem Backpack]], and Incline [[ASIN:B007E706K6 High Sierra Incline Backpack]]. I'm a 5'2" woman. For my uses (carryon for travel/day hikes), I selected the Neo model. This pack has alot of extra features, but some are useless. Best added feature of this pack is the raincover. I liked the 2 separate shoulder straps on this model as opposed to the yoke straps on 2 other models. All 4 packs had tags indicating that they could hold a 17" laptop. This model and the Incline could not hold my Dell 17" Inspiron. All 4 packs had pouches in the shoulder straps. The pouch in this one was useless. It was the smallest pouch and did not fit my iphone. Three of the models including this one, had a larger and probably more durable zippers than the Incline model. The padding on the bottom seems the same on all models. The raincover on this Access pack provides some extra padding when the raincover is in the hidden pouch. The padding on the backs of the packs seem to be about the same. I didn't use the packs, so I can't comment on the ventilation/airflow materials at the back of the packs.

Pros:
- Fabric seems durable
- Purple print is great color. Like the black accent.
- Raincover - nice feature. Easy on and off pack. Easy to store in bottom of pack.
- 2 unattached shoulder strips (unlike the yoke straps on other models which I don't like)
- Waist straps can be hidden in area at back of pack when not used.
- Chest straps location can be adjusted up and down about 2 inches
- Back access zipper for getting laptop in/out of pack
- 3 looped Daisy chain for attaching accessories to the front of the pack
- 1 attached Swivel Clip on front for adding gear
- Adjustable side compression straps
- Larger and hopefully more durable zippers on this model (smaller ones on Incline model)
- Comfortable grab handle on top of pack that is not integrated as part of shoulder straps.

Cons:
- Sternum/Chest straps not comfortable location for a 5'2" woman
- Waist straps not comfortable location for a 5'2" woman. Too low.
- Only 1 mesh pocket on outside. Why not add one on other side?
- Mess pocket on holds one 16-20 oz bottles nicely. For 1000 ml nalgene bottle, it stretches too much and doesn't go deep enough to be secure.
- Too Tight of a fit for my 17" Dell Inspiron Computer. (16.5" L x 11.5) Zipper does close at top (barely), but concerned it will cause pack to rip. Fits 15" Dell (15"x10").
- Hard to zip because of the flap over the zippers. If you fold the flap up, then zip the pack, then fold the flap back down, it makes the zipping easier but slower. IMO, this flap is unnecessary since the pack comes with a raincover.
- Detachable pouch for MP3 player or phone (Barely 4"x3"). Concerned it may come off causing whatever is in it to get broken or lost. Pouch is too small for iphone - Velcro closure flap cannot be closed.
- Vapel(tm) mesh Airflow(tm) padded shoulder straps are too stiff and uncomfortably dig into my body
- No zippered side pockets
- Smaller than expected. Fully loaded, not counting the mesh side pocket, it measures 19"x13"x10" = 2470 cu in. Less than the reported 2743.
text_fidelity_b: High Sierra Access Laptop Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
FILA Accessories Strength Band I have been through a lot this last year and having the ability to do quick exercises on the go is important. I have to go slowly and work up again to build up my body due to some issues and getting these strength bands is just the thing that I needed.

WHAT ARE THESE STRENGTH BANDS LIKE?
FILA strength bands come in a pretty sturdy box (significant because you can store them in there if you like). There are three bands that are color coded so it is easy to quickly identify their strength resistance when you need to grab one. The purple is light, the blue is medium, and the gray is heavy resistance. Along with the bands which each come individually wrapped are two paper fold outs. One has tips and warnings, and the other has a few exercise ideas of what you can do with these bands. I did notice that there is not a huge offensive smell with these bands either, so I wanted to point that out for anyone who might be concerned about that.

HOW DO THESE BANDS PERFORM?
Because I have to build up slowly, I have only been able to work up to the light resistance band at this point. At first the band seems as if it will not stretch that long as I am about 5ft 7in tall. I was particularly interested in doing the exercises which use the foot and require the arms to stretch above the head extended all of the way up. As I keep using the bands, they loosen up, however, and then they are perfect for whatever exercises that I want to use them for.

MY IMPRESSIONS OF THIS PACKAGE
To be honest, although I love the bands so far, I am a bit disappointed in the lack of exercises ideas included in this kit. I really would have like it if they included more ideas of what exercises to do with this band. I do realize that it is possible to look these up on the internet to find more exercises, but I would have liked it to be included in the set.

As for the bands, so far it is easy to hold and use, and I am finding my arms and shoulders are getting stronger which is just what I wanted.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Easy to hold and work with once they are broken in, these bands are a great way to do quick exercises to build strength. Color coded for easy identification, the quality of the bands seems to be solid so far. I only wish that more exercise ideas had been included in the box.

If I could, I would give these four and a half stars, but I can't so I am giving them five stars with the statement that better insert included with more exercises would make this much nicer than it is. But the bands themselves are great, so I plan to look up more exercises.
text_fidelity_b: FILA Accessories Strength Band

text_fidelity_a:
Bulk 120 Piece 4" Glow Stick with Cord Assortment - Ideal For Halloween, New Years, Dances or Emergencies While I was initially very happy to find a pack of 120 glowsticks with strings for a single price, I was less happy to receive the package and discover a grand total of 115 usable glowsticks. There were 2 others that lacked the caps to allow you to tie the strings on, so there were, technically, 117 glowsticks in the package, but I don't regard those two as usable due to the missing caps. There were also 126 strings, though I don't really regard an additional 11 strings as making up for the missing 5 usable glowsticks.

If a company is not going to be packing an accurate amount of product, then they should not advertise by a specific count. I don't have a problem with items packaged by weight so long as that is how they are advertised. This company should have advertised as "3 pounds of glowsticks with strings" or whatever weight it is instead of 120 glowsticks with strings as that is NOT what they delivered. From cheap ones to expensive ones. I always take them apart when I first get them and clean them, add oil where needed and inspect.

At this price, the action on this knife is amazing (see video). While the listing says ceramic bearings these are steel bearings for the pivot (see photos). It is still extremely smooth for deploy and for closing (even though it uses the tiny caged bearings, and they sit directly on the tang without grooves for said caged bearings).

The g10 is nicely textured with just enough checkering, and they are very slim scales which I appreciate as it is a bit bigger for a folder lengthwise. The slim scales give it a great feel and it really is very nice on the pocket and not as noticeable as other knives this length. The clip isn't ambidextrous however (but is tip up) and is right hand carry. It also isn't a deep carry clip but it works well enough (and there are many clips that would work with this 3-screw setup for the pocket clip).

I'm normally not a huge fan of tanto blade shapes but this has the tip grind elongated so that angle on this is much more usable, and looks better in my opinion. It could benefit from some jimping on the spine also, but this is minor.

The lockup is solid, with no wiggle even when getting the blade and pivot to a point where it drops shut.

Really a nice knife overall (and I can sometimes be critical with knives, specifically cheaper knives). At this price point it is really a great value and I'm glad to have received!
text_fidelity_b: Viwki Pocket Folding Knife with 3.34" Blade for Hunting Outdoor Tactical Survival and EDC,Handle w/Embossed Flag, Liner Lock, Flipper Open,Deep Carry Pocketclip

Reservoir & Bottle cleaner tablets (24 Tablets) | Water Bottle Cleaning Tablets Remove Stubborn Stains & Odors. Compatible with Hydration Bladders, Hydroflask, Camelbak, YETI, Thermos - Made in the USA Typically I would use bleach to clean my reservoirs, but it is fairly powerful and leaves an aftertaste if you aren't very careful. These have no such problem - one or two tabs, leave it overnight, takes care of everything for you. Gets rid of the biofilm that may have built up over months of storage, helps ensure that even after you've used your cleaning kit to get rid of visible buildup, you don't have other harmful organic particles floating around in there.

You can still use chlorine bleach on particularly tough cases, but one or two of these per year will do the trick on anything you usually use.

Wouldn't recommend using this to preserve water, though - they are a bit too strong for that. I use Katadyn Micropur MP1 tabs (ASIN: B000H3DNF4) for that purpose.

Speedo Aqua Fit Swim Training Gloves First of all, many thanks to all the other reviewers who mentioned that these run large. I wear a XL glove, so I was going to order this in XL. Very glad I didn't - the L size fits just fine, and now that I have one, it's clear the XL would have been too big. That tip from the other reviewers saved me some return postage - thanks!

In terms of the actual glove, it's great. Fits fine, and appears well made. Very secure velcro closure on the wrist.

I use mine for aqua aerobics and to add a "boost" to my swimming workouts. I've used the plastic hand paddle in the past - they are helpful in giving more resistance, but are rather awkward to use. These - if you'll forgive the inevitable pun - fit like a glove and don't get in the way. You can increase or decrease resistance by just expanding or closing your hand.

A word of caution - if you've never used hand paddles or webbed gloves before for exercise, go slow at first. You're putting a lot more strain on your muscles, especially the shoulders. Take it easy at first until you get a feel for the workout, then slowly increase duration and speed. A bit of care will prevent a lot of pain!

text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover Finally got a chance to take the bag out and put it though it’s paces. We don’t have any camping trips planned for now, but we put a towel and 10 lbs of weight and off we went. He’s 6 feet and skinny for reference. Took it for a thirty minute walk in 90 degrees F and 49% humidity. The pack felt good. The air gap was great, and kept him from overheating. He said the bag sat well and didn’t shift once secured. He is right handed and a lot like my other hiking backpacks, there is only a zipper pocket in the left waist band. This is because you don’t usually reach across to get something in your waist pocket on a hike. The right side is a non zip folded pocket. The rain cover stuffs in a Velcro pocket on the bottom and fits snugly over the entire pack. The large roomy main compartment fits everything I would need for a weekend hike, or a long day hike. Food, camp stove, change of clothing, single man tent, jacket and the large capacity reservoir. There is a hook to put the reservoir on so it doesn’t slip down as you empty the bladder. The bite valve is the standard camelback with shut off (this is important if you have ever been hiking and broken your bite valve and didn’t have time to dig out a spare until base camp.) this is Not a carry your laptop and tootle around town pack. This is a well made solid day/weekend hiker. Yes it would be nice to have a small inner zip pocket, but that’s what carabiners and dry sacks are for. It has a mesh two compartment pocket, and a larger pocket the whole bag length. Water reservoir has its own zippered compartment, and there is one center small zip pocket for quick access item like headlamp. Has a large adjustable mesh pocket on the outside that you can put a helmet, or ground roll. Can’t wait for camping to open up again, I may just steal this from my husband for scout campouts. Product free in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover

text_fidelity_a:
Renegade GK Talon Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 5-11, 5 Styles, Level 3) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 3.5+3MM Hyper Grip XD | Durable Goalkeeper Glove for All-Around Play | Based in The USA Update, 1 Let me say customer service is a 5 Star easily, prompt, courteous, and willing to make it right. We are well into our second pair of gloves at this point (got them in AUG, now Dec), and they have held up much better. However, the sticky factor is long gone as the material doesn't seem to keep that aspect. I purchased a bottle of GloveGlu which has fixed that issue.

I have increased the review to three stars, had the initial pair of gloves been as good as the second pair this would be a 4 star review. I think it odd, that the "pattern" in these reviews is the first pair of gloves tend to be less than quality, and then the second pair meets expectations. I would suggest that whoever is "making" the gloves need to improve their quality inspection as they gloves do not seem to be meeting the owners expectations, and it can't be good for the bottom line of the company to continue to reissue new gloves and give discounts on the original purchase to make it right. We purchase a new set every year, if the product would have had the quality of the second issue, I would have bought next years set from this company; however, given the pattern of the reviews, that may not be the case.

Once again customer service was 5 star, in the end the review is about the product, customer service should have never been involved nor a second pair of gloves. That combined with the pattern of the reviews, I feel 3 star (for this experience) is justified.

A bit disappointed in the gloves, we bought on May 18th it is now July 24th and they seem to showing signs of wear already the last set of gloves didn't show for 8 months or so. They also do not seem as "sticky" as the previous pair.

With that said my 11 year old plays year round both indoor and out, uses the gloves three times a week for practice plus 1-2 games a weekend. Seems as if he is dropping more balls than he use to as they gloves don't seem to have kept their grip. So now I am stuck with either paying $15 - $30 bucks for some glove stick or applying that amount toward another pair of gloves 2 months after these were purchases.

All in all fairly disappointed in the gloves.

UPDATE: WOW! What Customer Service, within two days of this post, I heard from the owner of the company who believed the gloves could have been defective AND he sent overnight a new pair so my son would have them for his weekend games.

I am certainly eager to see how the new set of gloves wear this go around and really hope they are as good as the customer service. Will Update later.
text_fidelity_b: Renegade GK Talon Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 5-11, 5 Styles, Level 3) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 3.5+3MM Hyper Grip XD | Durable Goalkeeper Glove for All-Around Play | Based in The USA

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included) I'm a long-time Fitbit user. I started out with my all-time favorite, the One, which was totally accurate and counted stairs. I replaced it with a Zip, which was also totally accurate but didn't count stairs, and mine went through batteries fast. I owned a couple Altas, that weren't accurate at all and I hated the charging cable.

And that brings me to the Inspire, which I'm pretty happy with. I'm going to start with the things I like about it.

I like the face options and how easy they are to change, the touchscreen - once you get used to it, it's very informative and easy to use, and I like the build quality, which is much nicer than the Zip for the same price I paid for the Zip a few years ago. I guess I got lucky - the unit uses about 10% of the battery per day. I very much prefer the way the Inspire docks in its charging cable - such an improvement over the Alta clips cable! And I've always had good luck getting support from Fitbit - when I had questions about the Inspire, I used their live chat and the rep was helpful and took her time.

Now for a neutral. My Inspire is reasonably accurate but not dead on. If I take 50 steps, it'll count 54 or 47. I can live with that. My One and Zip spoiled me, but both Altas were WAY off, which made me stop using a Fitbit for a while - no sense in wearing one if the counts are off by 25% to 30% (which they were).

There are cons. My first one only applies if you're a long-time Fitbit user and are used to using the wireless dongle so your Fitbit can communite with your computer. You won't be able to use the dongle because the Inspire uses Bluetooth rather than wireless to connect. I liked syncing with my computer, but opted to just sync with my phone as you now have to create a Microsoft account in order to download Fitbit Connect.

I found the band impossible to put on, but I mostly wear it on a clip, and there are some much easier to close and more attractive third-party bands for it on Amazon. It didn't recognize me cycling, and while that didn't bother me, it's worth noting - it would have been cool if that feature had worked.

My Inspire has made me a happy camper. I like wearing a Fitbit, seeing my steps and active minutes - that's why I've owned them. I find the Fitbit dashboard info and the quick stats on the screen motivating, and while I loved my One, the display on the Inspire gives more info more easily thanks to the touchscreen. I like the menus on the Inspire itself, the touchscreen and the charger. Oh, and I think the price ($58 when I bought it) is quite reasonable and a good value. I'm glad I got it :)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire Fitness Tracker, One Size (S and L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag The title tells you right up front this is a starter set, which is good to set expectations. It's not a huge set for the entire family, and it's aimed more for kids (though not little ones) than adults.

Packaging: Come in a long, thin box. stakes, mallet handles, mallet heads, balls are wrapped in plastic.

"Assembly": Really none. You have to screw the mallet handle into the mallet heads and that's it. They go in smoothly and easily, but if you plan on using the box to store the set, I suggest not tightening them too much as they can be hard to take apart once you've done so (a good thing for playing, less so for storing).

Construction:
Mostly they look nice. One of my wooden stakes had a small chip in it which is noticeable but honestly doesn't bother me much for an outdoor game. That was the only marring. The paint job is mostly fine though some are a little smudged or not neatly lined, but you'd have to really look at it to notice.

The mallets are short for adults (even for 5'4" me), so I'd say this is more for kids. Adults can certainly use them, but it'd definitely wear on my back after a while. They're also light and a bit thin, which makes me think they were purposely designed for kids in terms of size, ease of swing, and little concern about force. The balls and wickets are fine.

My only complaint would be storage. To use the box you have to disassemble the mallets each time and I'd be a little concerned about the wooden threads (especially with kids) over time. Plus, boxes tend to decay/get flimsy over time. So a carry bag of some sort, even a cheap one, would have been nice to throw in.

Outside of that, this is as it says, a basic starter set, mostly for older kids though anyone can use with varying ease/discomfort, and the price makes it a solid if not great value.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag

OMOLA Hoverboard seat Attachment, for 6.5”-10” Hoverboard, go Kart Conversion kit, Accessory for self Balancing Scooter, Transform Your Hoverboard into a go cart The look on my kids' faces when they tried this out was priceless- the same look they gave me when trying a hoverboard for the first time! It's a ton of fun, and far less likely to fall off and get hurt with, which I really like about it. You can also go faster more often without fear of falling off, something I never personally could do on the regular hoverboard (I rarely ever let it get up to full speed).
A couple of caveats:
1) Our board is self-balancing and detects when you get on/off, but having this setup attached to it confuses the sensors. Sometimes it sort of drifts if no one is on it since the residual weight is detected as a person pushing forward. It's also difficult to power off since the board thinks a person is still on it and refuses to power down unless I lift up on the kart so it thinks the weight has shifted.
2) The front part is a little wobbly. Not a deal breaker, but I'm afraid it will wear out more over time. Wish that was more solid.

I also had an issue trying it out inside where the entire front end came off and I slid along the floor of our playroom destroying a part of the vinyl flooring. This was really my fault because a) I didn't realize there are holes the tightening gear goes into, I just thought it held on with pressure until I flipped the bar over and saw the pre-drilled setting holes. And b) this should really NOT have been used indoors. Like, at all. I was being a big kid and now I have a gash in my floor I need to deal with somehow. But if you're not an idiot like me, you'll have a ton of fun with a compatible hoverboard under this!
text_fidelity_b: OMOLA Hoverboard seat Attachment, for 6.5”-10” Hoverboard, go Kart Conversion kit, Accessory for self Balancing Scooter, Transform Your Hoverboard into a go cart

Tents for Camping: Sportneer Tent for 2/3 Persons Family Pop Up Instant Tents Waterproof with Removable Top Rainfly Easy Set Up Tent 94.5"x86.6"x59" [[VIDEOID:64c8658b81382127e4a89d8e490ca985]] My kids love camping, so when we got this tent they were excited to try popping it up in our playroom first before we take it out. Before I go any further, I want to point out that to its' credit, this tent was easy enough for a couple of girls aged 9 and 11 to figure it out themselves.
That being said, I'm glad we did it at home first because I noticed at least one weird design flaw: The outer door cover is REALLY difficult to close from the inside. You see, like many tents, the doors are two layers: an outer rain flap and an inner bug-net window screen. bug net opens in the middle with a zipper, and the outer later opens on the sides (attached from the top, zipper around the perimeter).
This is odd because it seems like it is only designed to be closed from the outside like this! The zipper for the outer flap has an inside handle, but if the bug screen is closed, you can't reach it. I suppose you could open the bug screen all the way in order to get to the zipper, but it seems a whole lot easier to close and open both from the outside than the inside, which I wasn't expecting.
I'm not sure how I feel about that, I suppose it will still do the job out at a campsite, but it just feels poorly thought out.
text_fidelity_b: Tents for Camping: Sportneer Tent for 2/3 Persons Family Pop Up Instant Tents Waterproof with Removable Top Rainfly Easy Set Up Tent 94.5"x86.6"x59"

SYLVANIA RX2 OSRAM LED Bicycle Taillight This is a 2.4 lux/4 lumen rain proof and splash proof bicycle taillight which takes 2 AAA batteries (not included). These batteries should provide 36 hours of illumination according to the package.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this light. First, it's practically impossible to remove the cover to insert the batteries. There's a notch at the bottom of the light that is used to open the compartment. I had to use a letter opener to pry it open while squeezing the top a bit. The force that had to be used damaged the plastic around the notch but did not affect the light's functionality. There are four plastic prongs that hold the top reflector onto the base and I can see these prongs breaking when opening or closing the compartment to replace the batteries.

I have a Trek bike and it was difficult to position on my bike because the height of the light got in the way of the reflector that was already there. However, the mounting bracket is a typical bracket that clenches itself around the bike frame. The light clips onto the fastener and can be removed and used elsewhere, such as clipping onto a backpack or hat for use when walking.

The light turns on via a button on the back. Only the top "bulging" part lights up as the bottom acts as a reflector.

Because of the difficulty of opening this light and chance for breakage during battery replacement, I personally cannot recommend this. This is not a light I would purchase after having tried it.
text_fidelity_b: SYLVANIA RX2 OSRAM LED Bicycle Taillight

text_fidelity_a:
Thule SUP Taxi XT Surfboard Rack This is just fantastic quality and design, as I've come to expect from Thule. Seems that you just can't find a better product. And in this case, I'm not sure anyone else makes carriers specifically for stand up paddleboards. It has a smooth and super slick width adjusting system, and it adjusts so much that you can pile two boards in this setup with a divider between them for protection.

It seems there is a thin, steel braided cable inside the strap to deter casual thieves (although I could cut it with a good diagonal cutters, which is probably something I could find in my trunk, but perhaps only because I like tools). Anyway, I think that and the included locking cylinders make this about the most secure setup that you can get.

Speaking of the locking cylinders, they use the same type of keys as my other Thule stuff. But you'll have to special order them separately if you want to have on key for all your gear. I don't know of any program to make this easier on you, but it would be great if they just gave you a voucher for new locking cylinders if you have already registered one of their other products or something like that. I'm actually not certain if you can remove them once you put them in...

The only thing I don't like is the nylon rope to hold the front of the boards down. I mean, I just don't like having to use this cumbersome and annoying, old-style method, but this is just inherent to hauling boards and there's really nothing Thule can do about it (although you never know what they'll come up with). This is just a physics problem that hasn't been completely solved.

Yeah, the materials are perfect, the design is well-thought out and specific. You just really can't beat this thing. It is impressive in its own right. It's for sure on the top end of what I want to pay, but it is nice to have the best.
text_fidelity_b: Thule SUP Taxi XT Surfboard Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Contigo Fit Autospout Water Bottle 32oz, Surge When I examined this water bottle's product picture, I wrongly assumed that it was constructed of stainless steel like my other Contigo water bottle because, in appearance, they look exactly the same, with the same dark color. Unfortunately, this water bottle is made of plastic, inside and out.

The claim from the manufacturer is that this plastic is BPA free. Perhaps this will be reassuring enough for many consumers to be willing to purchase this water bottle. However, my understanding, based on my own personal research on the subject, is that there is no such thing as any type of plastic that does not to some extent leach chemicals into any water one puts into a plastic container. So plastic water bottles are a problem for me. However, since the manufacturer did not outright lie about the plastic, only buried it in the bowels of the product description such that I completely missed it, I will not strongly downgrade my rating for that.

There is another issue with this water bottle, though, that is also an issue for me personally. The lid requires one to suck water out through a short, straw-like top. This will require use of a straw-cleaning, slender brush in order to adequately clean it, and the manufacturer does not provide such a brush along with this water bottle.

The lid will also need to be soaked in warm, soapy dishwater along with the water bottle itself after every use in order to avoid the build-up of mold. However, since every water bottle is ideally treated that way, I will not grade down this water bottle for needing to be washed very carefully.

The one advantage a plastic water bottle has over a stainless steel one is that, in some cases, it can be lighter in weight. I will admit that my stainless steel Contigo water bottle is heavier in weight than this plastic one. But the way to prevent that from being a problem is to simply not fill a stainless-steel water bottle completely full, or, better yet, purchase one that isn't huge and unwieldy in size.
text_fidelity_b: Contigo Fit Autospout Water Bottle 32oz, Surge

I have 30" snowshoes and decided to purchase this large bag that fits 36" snowshoes because I could not find a medium size in this quality. Tubbs does sell a medium bag for 30" snowshoes but I was unable to find it on Amazon.

This bag is strong and has one tiny inside pocket that would hold a flip phone, money, or Chapstick. Although the interior will fit other items such as a change of clothes, jacket, etc.; those items would be mixed in with the snowshoes and perhaps would get damaged by them.

The side of the bag has two Velcro straps for holding the snowshoe / trekking poles. What I don't like about these straps (or any straps like these) is that the poles will slip down. I actually clip my poles into a spacer and that spacer catches onto the top strap so that they don't slip down.

The other side has a handle so that it can be carried like a guitar case. It also has backpack straps which is the way I prefer to carry my snowshoes.

I attached two pictures of the bag without the poles and one with the poles attached. Note that I am unable to collapse my poles so I leave them extended. However, the best way to travel with the poles on this bag is to collapse them first before strapping them on. I also attached a picture of the back of the bag that shows the backpack handles and side handle.
text_fidelity_b: Tubbs Snowshoes Snowshoe Bag

Cat Caterpillar Camo Hydration Reservoir -2L We don't hike per se, but we do head out to the ranch in the deep West Texas borderlands a couple of times a year and you absolutely need water on your person out there. The Chihuahua desert and Chinati mountains combined with extreme temperatures out there can cause a serious hydration problem very quickly. Typically, I put two one gallon containers per person in our saddle bags and we ride out. I like the idea of having this water pouch for walking with it's built in straw.

The pouch itself is easy to see with clear sections in the camo print so you know exactly how much water you have left. The straw has a pull off cover and it pops back into place with a firm click so you know it's really closed. The fill opening is wide enough to refill with a water hose or just using the regular old kitchen faucet. I was surprised that the pouch has absolutely no plastic or chemical scent whatsoever.

My problem is the lack of velcro or any sort of straps to attach it to a backpack or belt. Basically, you have to carry it or already have a backpack with existing straps or a pocket available to hold a water pouch. It this had an attached loop even on the top, I could clip it my saddle or my jacket - I rarely use a backpack when on horseback so we'll have to retrofit something to this.
text_fidelity_b: Cat Caterpillar Camo Hydration Reservoir -2L

I had to wait until the next day to use them again. I can see where they would be beneficial but I will be using them more carefully.

From what I have been able to tell all three bands are exactly the same. Usually when there is more than one color, belt, or band there is different resistance. This allows the user to slowly build up strength to move on to the next band. This is not the case with these Resistance bands.

If you have not been working out or you have not been strengthening the muscles used with these bands use should use caution. Injury to knees and hips are inevitable.

There is a small insert with what exercises you can do using these bands but there is NO caution on how an injury is possible.

I will not be recommending these resistance bands to family and friends. The chance for injury is too high.

text_fidelity_a:
Walker's Razor Slim The things I was curious about before buying these:
A) How they sound.
B) How they feel.
C) Compared to Howard Leights by Honeywell as well as the BT edition of the Walker Razor.

I have not tested the Noise Cancellation yet but provided it works as it should I wanted to get out my review in case anyone wondered what I did. My hand's on impressions have been fully positive.
If you get these and wonder how to open the package: I just bent the package in half. This caused the cardboard to split open and the plastic clamshell is not sealed - it is 2 parts and the headphones came out super simple.

How do they sound? (I own Sennheiser HD600 compared to those:)
A)Surprisingly good. Not audiophile but not bad.
B)Bass is light. Not much bass from these. Bass seems purposely reserved, truth be told probably neutral.
C)Slight emphasis on mid-range. But not annoying in any frequency.
D)Highs are present but not pristine.
E)Overall, they sound good for a $43 set of headphones that do so much more. I am pleased with it. I can listen without irritation.

How do they feel?
A) A little tight on my medium-sized head but the muffs are plushy and do a good job of distributing the clamp pressure.
B) I can't imagine wearing these for much more than an hour at a time but it might be ok for longer but probably no one will actually want to.
C) Headband doesn't rub my scalp.
D) No hair pulling or "pinchy parts".
E) The hinges that hold the muffs look thin but they work (so far). Durability could be a concern.
F) The hinges are adjustable. I collapsed then down about 2/5ths of the way so they could possibly fit larger heads but wider heads may have more clamp pressure?
G) Again, the clamp pressure is pretty tight. I am surprised how tight they are. But they stay on the head when moving my head which is good. It is a good thing they are tight but it could cause them to fatigue your head after a while. Be aware they are pretty tight on the head but I don't believe it will be a deal-breaker.

How is the enhanced hearing:
A) Fairly natural. I can rather accurately distinguish sounds.
B) I never knew what a bee flying sounded like other than Bumblebees right in my ear. I heard the bee and I will learn that sound but I wouldn't have known what it was had I not seen the bee and heard the sound.
C) You will discover new sounds you haven't heard before.
D) Unfortunately, the sound is mono-sounding like everyone has said. Determining the origin or placement of noises does not work out so well.
E) I questioned whether to get these or the Howard Leight by Honeywell. I decided to try these first after listening to YouTube videos. I have read reviews that say the "Howard's" better determine which direction noises come from but some videos said they do not do it better enough to choose them over these.
F) These are supposedly more comfortable than the Howard Leights.
G) They are cheaper and look better IMO than the Howard Leights.
H) I might buy the Howard Leights just to see if the sound placement is better because I think that would be a big deal but from what I have read and heard the hype may or may not be all it is cracked up to be. The reviewers mostly chose these over the Howard Leight.

Overall, I am impressed that these are only $43.
Be sure to get a 3.5mm to 3.5mm male to male wire to use them for music.
I wanted to get the Bluetooth version but after reading how much problems people were having with the BT dropping or not working, I decided to get the wired version.
The BT version has 4 mics which, on paper, seems would give better awareness of surroundings but from things I heard it didn't quite work as well in RL as it seems it would. I still would like to try those because it would be worth the money to me if they worked like they should but if they didn't I knew I would still be getting these.
text_fidelity_b: Walker's Razor Slim

text_fidelity_a:
sixthreezero Electric-Bicycles Around The Block Women's Ebike, 250/500 Watt Motor, 7-Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle with Rear Rack, 26" Wheels, Multiple Colors This review is for the sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Step-Through 500-Watt Electric Bike

The short version is: This is a great bike, sixthreezero has great support, and I highly recommend the bike and company.

My mom has some back issues, including fused vertebrae, and over the years, the number of physical activities she's able to participate in has declined. Long family bike rides on a normal bike were no longer an option. For that reason, in February we decided to go to a local Pedego store and rent e-bikes for my mom and wife. We did a 15 mile ride, and everyone, including my mom and wife, loved it.

My mom liked it so much that she reconfirmed the prices when we got back, but it was definitely outside of her budget.

We both spent the next several months looking for an e-bike deal that was too good to say no to. There's some cheap options online, a Costco mountain e-bike, some nice bikes that are out of our budget, both online and locally, but nothing that was amazing...

Until Prime Day 2019.

sixthreezero's 250-watt bikes were on sale during Prime Day. I don't even see them available now, but it was a great deal, and I did some research before phoning my mom and telling her I think we'd found the deal she was looking for. After telling my mom about it, she ordered one, then asked if I was getting one for my wife. I was on the fence, because it's still a lot of money, until she said, "Don't think about how much you're spending per ride. Do you want to have lots of happy memories of the family riding together or are you OK without those?"

Well said, Mom. I ordered one the next day.

Now, I don't see the 250-watt bikes on Amazon anymore, but when they were here, the online documentation, both here and over at sixthreezero at the time we ordered made the basic functionality seem the same between the 250-watt and the 500-watt bicycles. The key feature both my mom and wife were looking for was the ability to pedal with adjustable resistance, but leverage the throttle with the left thumb to accelerate with the motor when needed to either catch up quickly or tackle hills without issue. (And without changing the level of pedal assistance.)

Some of our first impressions were not great. My mom's bike showed up looking amazing, and my dad assembled it without issue, but the throttle did not behave as expected. (The boost was limited to the level of pedal assist you were in.) My wife's bike showed up, but the fender and rack were both badly bent.

Before buying the bike, I saw that sixthreezero, if you bought directly from them, was willing to offer 365 day test drives, and seemed really focused on customer satisfaction. The Amazon reviews seemed positive, and the box the bike came in offered free assembly at a local bike store. (I'm not sure how that works because I've built over a dozen bikes and this bike is easy to assemble.) That said, I had a damaged bike and it didn't perform as I was expecting. I was definitely concerned when I reached out to sixthreezero.

After multiple calls, photos and a video to confirm that my 250-watt bike did not perform the way their 500-watt did (the technician I was working with only had a 500-watt readily available to troubleshoot with), they were willing to work with my mom and I to find a satisfactory proposal that would allow us to send back the 250-watt bikes and they would ship us 500-watt versions.

They were polite and reasonable throughout the process, but I was still nervous about bike number two, since the first bike did arrive with issues outside of the e-bike functionality. I was pleasantly surprised that they seem to have people working there who seem to genuinely want to make sure their customers love their bikes.

The 500-watt bike went together very easily, and after assembling and tuning the bike, I took it for a ride. The bike was a blast.

The only thing that jumped out at me as being substantially different from the Pedego my wife rode was the seat post. The Pedego had a shock in the seat post, which doesn't do a lot, but is better than nothing. I ordered a "Sunlite Pillar Suspension Seat Post, 27.2 x 350mm, Silver" from Amazon, which seemed like a good improvement to the bike, which is otherwise fantastic. (The rigid seat post makes the ride a tad rough, which is why I gave comfort 4 stars, I'd bump that to 5 with the suspension seat post.)

My wife says she finds the sixthreezero 500-watt basically the same as the Pedego. I'm sure there are differences, but the only big one we see is the price.

I can't adequately describe an e-bike in words alone, but if you have the option to rent one locally, I highly suggest you try it. It's a lot of fun. I'm not a fan of skilled cyclists tearing up mountain bike trails with heavier, faster e-bikes, nor would I advocate road bikers throw electric motors on their bikes, but the joy e-bikes are able to bring families by leveling the field for families that want to ride together is awesome. And sixthreezero's EVRYjourney cruiser is a fantastic bike for those people.

We're averaging speeds of more than half a mile per hour more as a family than we used to, and my wife comes home with a smile on her face while my kids come home having used up more energy and me having gotten a better work out. I know this bike is not cheap, but I like the way my mom put it to me:

Would you rather be out riding with your loved ones? This is a fantastic option for those who can't match the speed or stamina of the people they're riding with.
text_fidelity_b: sixthreezero Electric-Bicycles Around The Block Women's Ebike, 250/500 Watt Motor, 7-Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle with Rear Rack, 26" Wheels, Multiple Colors

text_fidelity_a: Stamina 35-1215 Orbital Rowing Machine with Free Motion Arms - Smart Workout App, No Subscription Required After using a Concept2 Model D rowing machine at a gym and getting great fitness results, I decided I would get a rowing machine for home as well.  Installation of the Stamina 1215 did not take too long and was relatively easy to follow the directions.  However, always check and tighten screws and bolts to ensure a safe workout because once or twice I noticed issues such as a screw on the floor or loose arms.  The electronic monitor is not high quality as the face is not securely fastened to the battery box.  If moved or during rigorous training sessions, the face could fall off or there could be issues with it functioning properly so it's not always reliable.  I have not been as motivated to use the Stamina rower because it's hard to get the level or resistance I want-- it's either too much, not the same on both sides, or doesn't feel like it's giving me a similar workout as the gym's rower.  Also, the seat is not as comfortable for my 30+ minute workouts.  Although it is 3-4 times more expensive, my next purchase will be a Concept2 Model D rowing machine.
text_fidelity_b: Stamina 35-1215 Orbital Rowing Machine with Free Motion Arms - Smart Workout App, No Subscription Required

text_fidelity_a: Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack A very sturdy product that is made quite well. Only reason I am not giving this a higher rating is due to the rubber attachment on the stabilizer arm. The majority of the weight is kept on the big foam pad that goes on the lid of your trunk, the smaller arm with the rubber end is on top of the trunk for support/balance. I am not sure why these guys chose this material but it was a mistake. If you use this product regularly, that rubber is going to dull your paint. I now have a nice dull patch where the rubber met the trunk which is extremely annoying. It's not like the rack was loose and constantly swayed, it was tightly secured. Every other manufacturer uses foam for all weight bearing arms, from what I have seen in stores. In retrospect I should have gone with the popular trend and gotten something else.
text_fidelity_b: Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack
